chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Uthman ibn Isa, from al-Samma' ibn Mihran, who said: I asked him

about a man who incurred janabah (major ritual impurity) during the night in Ramadan, so he slept knowing about it, and did not wake up until dawn overtook him. He said: He must complete his fast and make up one other day. I said: If that is the case for the man while he is making up the days of Ramadan? He said: Let him eat on that day and make it up, for it is not like Ramadan; none of the months are like Ramadan.

key_terms.الْفَجْر: Dawn, the time for the Fajr prayer and fasting beginning
key_terms.جَنَابَة: Major ritual impurity requiring full body wash
key_terms.رَمَضَان: The month of fasting in the Islamic calendar
key_terms.يَقْضِي: To make up for a missed obligatory act

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person who sleeps in a state of janabah until dawn during Ramadan?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *al-Istibsar*, highlighting the juristic distinction between the obligatory fast of Ramadan and the compensatory fast (*qada*). The Imam clarifies that while the Ramadan fast remains valid despite sleeping in a state of *janabah* until dawn, the make-up day is treated as a regular month's fast rather than a direct substitute for Ramadan, implying different ritual nuances for the *qada* day.
